target: Avrei voluto venire alla festa.
english: I would have liked to come to the party.
tip: Past conditional = conditional of avere or essere plus the participle. Avrei voluto = 'I would have liked', a past regret.

target: A loro piacerebbe viaggiare di più.
english: They'd like to travel more.
tip: With piacere the person who likes is the indirect object: a loro piacerebbe = literally 'to them it would please'.

target: Stasera cucinerò la pasta alla carbonara.
english: Tonight I'll cook pasta carbonara.
tip: Spoken Italian often uses the present for the future: instead of cucinerò you could just say 'stasera cucino'.

target: Marco troverà sicuramente un buon lavoro.
english: Marco will definitely find a good job.
tip: Buono shortens to buon before a masculine singular noun: un buon lavoro, just like the article un.

target: Potrei venire alla festa sabato sera.
english: I could come to the party Saturday night.
tip: For 'on Saturday' use sabato with no preposition. Adding the article, il sabato, would mean 'every Saturday'.

target: Gradirei ricevere maggiori informazioni sul corso.
english: I'd appreciate receiving more information about the course.
tip: Informazioni is normally plural in Italian, unlike English 'information': maggiori informazioni = more information.

target: Dove andresti se potessi vivere ovunque?
english: Where would you go if you could live anywhere?
tip: Andare contracts its future and conditional stem to andr-: andresti = 'you would go', not andaresti.

target: È esattamente quello che mi serviva, grazie!
english: It's exactly what I needed, thanks!
tip: Quello che means 'what', the thing that: quello che mi serviva is 'what I needed', with no specific noun behind it.

target: Rimarrei a Roma per sempre se potessi.
english: I'd stay in Rome forever if I could.
tip: Use a with cities and towns: a Roma = 'in/to Rome'. Countries take in instead, as in in Italia.

target: Bastava che tu mi avvisassi in anticipo.
english: You just needed to let me know in advance.
tip: Bastava che ('it was enough that') triggers the subjunctive: bastava che tu mi avvisassi.

target: Dovresti parlare con il tuo capo di questo.
english: You should talk to your boss about this.
tip: Parlare con means to talk with a person; parlare di means to talk about a topic. Here both appear.

target: Il nuovo ponte verrà inaugurato la prossima primavera.
english: The new bridge will be inaugurated next spring.
tip: Italian also builds the passive with venire: verrà inaugurato = 'will be inaugurated', like sarà inaugurato.

target: La maggior parte delle persone preferirebbe lavorare da casa.
english: Most people would prefer to work from home.
tip: La maggior parte ('most') takes a singular verb even with a plural: la maggior parte delle persone preferirebbe.

target: Il dottore dal quale sono andato è molto bravo.
english: The doctor I went to see is very good.
tip: "Dal quale" – formal alternative to "da cui".

target: La famiglia i cui figli vanno alla stessa scuola.
english: The family whose children go to the same school.
tip: Cui means 'whose' between two nouns; the article agrees with the thing owned, not the owner: i cui figli.

target: Dovrei studiare di più per l'esame.
english: I should study more for the exam.
tip: Italian builds should from the conditional of dovere (must): dovrei studiare = I should study.

target: Lei sarebbe contenta di ricevere una visita.
english: She'd be happy to receive a visit.
tip: 'Lei' = she (or formal 'you'). Context determines which meaning. The verb form is the same for both.

target: Avrà circa quarant'anni.
english: He's probably about forty.
tip: The future can express a guess about the present: 'avrà quarant'anni' means he's probably about forty.

target: Terrò il tuo segreto, promesso.
english: I'll keep your secret, promise.
tip: tenere has an irregular future: the stem contracts to terr-, giving 'terrò', not 'tenerò'.

target: Verrò a trovarti appena possibile.
english: I'll come visit you as soon as possible.
tip: 'Venire a trovare' is the idiom for visiting someone: 'verrò a trovarti' = I'll come see you, not find you.

target: Il mese prossimo sarò in vacanza.
english: Next month I'll be on vacation.
tip: 'essere in vacanza' takes no article: 'sarò in vacanza' = I'll be on vacation, literally 'in vacation'.

target: Ti sposerai l'anno prossimo come previsto?
english: Will you get married next year as planned?
tip: 'sposarsi' (reflexive) = to get married; 'sposare' plus an object = to marry someone. Here 'ti sposerai'.

target: Entro maggio, saremo tornati dal viaggio.
english: By May, we'll have returned from the trip.
tip: 'Entro' (by a deadline) pairs with the future perfect: 'saremo tornati' = we'll have returned by then.

target: Ci rivedremo presto, ne sono sicuro.
english: We'll see each other again soon, I'm sure.
tip: Reciprocal reflexive: 'ci' means 'each other', so 'ci rivedremo' = we'll see each other again.

target: Dovrò lavorare anche domenica questa settimana.
english: I'll have to work on Sunday this week too.
tip: dovere builds its future by dropping the stem vowel: 'dovrò', not 'doverò'.

target: Questo è ciò di cui ho bisogno.
english: This is what I need.
tip: Avere bisogno takes di, so the relative pronoun carries that di with it: ciò di cui ho bisogno = the thing I need.

target: Non ha chiamato, il che è strano.
english: He didn't call, which is strange.
tip: 'il che' refers back to a whole statement, meaning 'which': 'non ha chiamato, il che è strano'.

target: Avevo già letto quel libro due volte.
english: I had already read that book twice.
tip: Trapassato prossimo with avere: 'avevo letto' = I had read, an action finished before another past point.

target: Non sarà facile, ma ce la farò.
english: It won't be easy, but I'll make it.
tip: 'farcela' means to manage or pull it off; the 'ce la' is fixed: 'ce la farò' = I'll make it.

target: Se non dormi abbastanza, sarai stanco domani.
english: If you don't sleep enough, you'll be tired tomorrow.
tip: Real condition: use the present after 'se' (dormi) and the future in the result (sarai stanco).
